clue.text: Resting place by river for rodent

blocks.note: a dorm, short for dormitory, is a room full of beds
beside: the next piece sits right after
the Ouse is an English river, a crossword favourite

explanation.surface: A rodent looking for somewhere to rest near the water.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ouse is a river in Yorkshire (and another in Sussex). A dormouse famously sleeps a lot, so the surface suits it.
explanation.definitionFit: The dormouse is a small hibernating rodent, an example of the class named.

clue.text: Medicate deer around south

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so the first piece wraps the second

blocks.note: a doe is a female deer
S is the abbreviation for south

explanation.surface: A vet treats a deer somewhere in the south.
explanation.definitionFit: To dose someone is to give them medicine, a verb synonym of medicate.

clue.text: Studies grasses when speaking

indicators.note: when speaking means the word is taken by how it is pronounced, not spelt

blocks.note: reeds are tall waterside grasses

explanation.surface: A botanist researches grasses and talks about them.
explanation.walkthrough: A student reads a subject at a British university, so 'reads' can mean studies.
explanation.definitionFit: To read a subject is British usage for studying it at university.

clue.text: Asking too much from grocer having bananas

indicators.note: going bananas means going crazy, so these letters run wild into a new order

blocks.note: the twelve letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A shopkeeper selling bananas puts the prices up too high.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bananas' looks like the grocer's stock, but it is the slang for crazy that signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Overcharging means demanding too high a price, which is asking too much.

clue.text: Injure artist during pirouette

indicators.note: during means in the middle of, so one piece sits inside the other

blocks.note: a pirouette is a spin on one foot
RA is a Royal Academician, a crossword artist

explanation.surface: A ballet dancer hurts themself mid-turn.
explanation.definitionFit: To sprain a joint is to injure it by wrenching the ligaments.

clue.text: Mailbags oddly depleted sadly

indicators.note: losing the odd-numbered positions leaves only the second, fourth, sixth and eighth characters

blocks.note: the even letters of the word, once the odd ones are dropped

explanation.surface: A postal worker laments that the mailbags have run strangely empty.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are sentence adverbs of regret: 'alas, it rained' means 'sadly, it rained'.

clue.text: Observing throne with head of state

blocks.note: 'the throne' is jokey slang for the toilet, and loo is British for toilet
a king is a head of state

explanation.surface: A monarch on the throne surveys the scene.
explanation.walkthrough: The royal throne is a decoy: the slang throne is the toilet, which Britons call the loo.
explanation.definitionFit: Looking and observing both mean directing your eyes at something.

clue.text: Hospital above city accepting time for purity

indicators.note: accepting means taking in, so one piece is received inside another

blocks.note: san is short for sanatorium
in a down clue, above places this piece first
taken as written
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A hospital overlooking the city stands for cleanliness.
explanation.definitionFit: Sanctity is holiness, and moral purity is close to its sense of sacred inviolability.

clue.text: Popular transport hub includes everything fitting

indicators.note: includes means contains, so one piece goes inside another

blocks.note: in means fashionable or popular
a railway or bus station is a transport hub
all means everything

explanation.surface: A busy station contains every facility you could want.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fitting' reads as an adjective meaning suitable, but it is the noun: the act of putting something in place.
explanation.definitionFit: Installation, like fitting, is the process of putting equipment in position.

clue.text: Scold son behind schedule

blocks.note: S is the standard abbreviation for son
running behind schedule means late

explanation.surface: A parent tells off a child who has come home late.
explanation.definitionFit: To slate someone is British informal usage for criticising them harshly, a synonym of scold.

clue.text: Work party with number initially being neglected

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the opening character of each of the two words before it is kept

blocks.note: to run a machine or business is to work it
a do is a social gathering
the first letters of these two words

explanation.surface: An office party grows in size while the workplace is left untended.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the definition as an adjective: a run-down building is one suffering from neglect.
explanation.definitionFit: Run-down describes a place in poor repair through lack of care, which is the state of something being neglected.

clue.text: Typist's chair adjusted for doctor

indicators.note: something adjusted has been altered and set differently, so these letters are reordered

blocks.note: the twelve letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: An office worker's chair is altered on medical advice.
explanation.definitionFit: A psychiatrist is a medically qualified specialist in mental illness, so a kind of doctor.

clue.text: Spice king perhaps meets a mother

blocks.note: a king is one example of a playing card
taken as written
mom is the American word for mother

explanation.surface: A spicy monarch is introduced to someone's mum.
explanation.definitionFit: Cardamom is an aromatic seed pod used in curries, an example of a spice.

clue.text: Ms Gardner and sailor in film

blocks.note: Ava Gardner was a Hollywood star
tar is an old word for a sailor

explanation.surface: An actress and a seaman share a screen in a movie.
explanation.definitionFit: Avatar is James Cameron's 2009 blockbuster, an instance of a film.

clue.text: A London orchestra managed without a place

definitions.note: a phrase describing the noun's situation

blocks.note: taken as written
LSO is the London Symphony Orchestra
ran means managed, as one runs a business

explanation.surface: An orchestra copes without a venue.
explanation.walkthrough: In racing, a horse that is 'placed' finishes in the first few; one that is not is an also-ran.
explanation.definitionFit: An also-ran is a racehorse or competitor finishing unplaced, hence one left without a place.

clue.text: Minor insult

blocks.note: first meaning: small, not important
second meaning: a snub or display of disrespect

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as a phrase about a small offence, but the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both an adjective for something small and a noun or verb for a deliberate snub.

clue.text: Entertain with revolting beer and ecstasy

indicators.note: revolting means rising up against order, so these letters break ranks and rearrange

blocks.note: lager is a type of beer
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A host keeps guests amused with nasty beer and party drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolting' looks like a verdict on the beer's taste, but it signals a rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: To regale people is to entertain them, typically with stories or lavish food.

clue.text: Bad-tempered beagle raised poorly

indicators.note: done poorly suggests a badly made job, so the letters come out in a jumbled order

blocks.note: the twelve letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A dog brought up badly turns out snappy.
explanation.definitionFit: A disagreeable person is unpleasant and irritable, a synonym of bad-tempered.

clue.text: Money is enticement across China's capital

indicators.note: across means spanning over, so one piece stretches around another
a word's capital is its head, so only the opening character is used

blocks.note: a lure is something that entices
the first letter of China

explanation.surface: A remark that cash is the bait drawing people to Beijing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'China's capital' wants to be Beijing, but here it means the first letter of the word China.
explanation.definitionFit: Lucre is money, especially when gained dishonourably, as in 'filthy lucre'.

clue.text: Regularly turnout for jog

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other character is taken

blocks.note: the first, third, fifth and seventh letters

explanation.surface: People often turn out to go running.
explanation.definitionFit: To trot is to run at a gentle pace, a synonym of jog.

clue.text: Girl missing in action hiding currency

indicators.note: to hide something is to keep it inside, so one piece is held within the other

blocks.note: MIA is the military abbreviation for missing in action
the rand is South Africa's currency

explanation.surface: A soldier's girl goes missing while concealing money.
explanation.definitionFit: Miranda is a girl's name, famously Prospero's daughter in The Tempest.

clue.text: Suffer again, cursing inwardly

indicators.note: inwardly points to the inside of the preceding words, where the solution sits

blocks.note: found across the end of one word and the start of the next

explanation.surface: Someone hurt a second time swears under their breath.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Again' tempts you toward a RE- word, but it is only part of the hiding place.
explanation.definitionFit: To incur a loss or penalty is to bring it on yourself and suffer it.

clue.text: Language of male getting cross

blocks.note: a man is a male person
X is the shape of a cross

explanation.surface: A man's speech turns angry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross' looks like an adjective for anger but stands for the letter shaped like a cross.
explanation.definitionFit: Manx is the Celtic tongue of the Isle of Man, revived in recent decades.

clue.text: Redesign opening on control

blocks.note: to rein in is to control
a vent is an opening for air

explanation.surface: A designer reworks a control panel's aperture.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across clue 'A on B' puts A after B, so the opening follows the control.
explanation.definitionFit: To reinvent something is to remake it in a new form, to redesign it.
